question: What is the LymphGen classification system, and how was it validated in the corpus?
gold_notes: Genetic subtype classifier for DLBCL (MCD, BN2, N1, EZB, ST2); validated on MSK 400-gene clinical NGS panel.

agentic.answer:
The [LymphGen](methods/LymphGen.html) classification system is a probabilistic algorithm that assigns diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) cases to one of six molecular subtypes (MCD, BN2, EZB, A53, ST2, N1) using SNVs, small INDELs, copy number alterations, and FISH translocation data.

In the corpus, it was validated in [PMID:38497151](papers/38497151.html) by applying LymphGen to 396 DLBCL cases sequenced with the MSK-IMPACT Heme panel (400 genes) plus BCL2/BCL6 FISH translocations. The study found:

- **92% overall accuracy** (86% sensitivity, 98% specificity) against a comprehensive NCI panel reference standard
- 55% of MSK cases were successfully classified; EZB (22%) was the most common subtype
- Restricting to high-confidence predictions (>90% probability) improved accuracy to 96%
- CNA data proved essential—removing it dropped accuracy to 81%, particularly affecting A53 subtype classification

This demonstrates LymphGen's applicability to clinical-grade targeted sequencing panels.

rag.answer:
# LymphGen Classification System and Validation

## What is LymphGen?

LymphGen is a probabilistic classification algorithm developed by the National Cancer Institute that subclassifies diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) into six molecularly distinct genetic subtypes: MCD, EZB, BN2, N1, ST2, and A53 (PMID:38497151). This system provides broader biological heterogeneity classification than the traditional ABC/GCB (activated B-cell/germinal center B-cell) paradigm and includes prognostic correlations (PMID:38497151).

## Validation Methodology

The corpus describes validation of LymphGen on a clinical 400-gene targeted NGS panel (MSK-IMPACT) used at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center:

**Performance on NCI Cohort (filtered to IMPACT genes):**
- Overall accuracy: 92% (86% sensitivity, 98% specificity) (PMID:38497151)
- In the "Core" group (high-confidence cases >90% probability): 96% accuracy, 83% sensitivity, 89% specificity (PMID:38497151)

**Application to MSK Clinical Cohort (396 DLBCL cases):**
- 55% of cases successfully classified into one of the six subtypes (PMID:38497151)
- About two-thirds of classified cases were in the "Core" group, one-third in the "Extended" group (50-90% probability) (PMID:38497151)

The study confirmed that genomic classifications using LymphGen can be effectively translated into routine clinical care using targeted NGS panels (PMID:38497151).
